kilauea.activity_summary: Episode 55 of the ongoing Halemaʻumaʻu eruption ended abruptly at 9:03 a.m. HST on October 17, 2026. VAN is being reissued to drop the alert level from WATCH to ADVISORY and the color code from ORANGE to YELLOW.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues. Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.

result.caveats: Kilauea was in episodic_pause, Episode 55 ended at 9:03 a.m. HST ~2 hr before the 11:00 a.m. HST (21:00Z) image, so plume may be residual or passive degassing and emission rate is uncertain. Upwind end is 35.7 km from Kilauea summit on the SE coast, not at the vent, likely due to cloud over the island obscuring the over-land portion and segmentation starting offshore. Visibility is faint, limiting color discrimination. Summit/flank thermal clusters are lava/vent glow, not proof of emissions on their own.
evidence: diffuse pale blue-gray haze extending south-southwest from southern Hawaii island over ocean, fainter and bluer than surrounding bright white clouds - typical vog, not bright textured cloud or brown smoke
177 km long plume orientation SSW is downwind of 10-m wind from 030 deg (NE) at 16.7 kmh at Kilauea summit
upwind end 35.7 km from Kilauea summit vs 69.6 km from Mauna Loa summit, favoring Kilauea; nearest non-volcanic fire cluster near Honolulu is 389.4 km distant

USGS HVO at image time: Kilauea ADVISORY/YELLOW episodic_pause with Episode 55 ending that morning plus 316 summit-caldera thermal exclusions indicating recent eruption/degassing, while Mauna Loa is NORMAL/GREEN not erupting
pale gray-blue diffuse haze south of Hawaii island, bluer and fainter than white clouds
SSW extent consistent with NE wind from 30 deg transporting summit emissions to the south-southwest
upwind end SE coast 35.7 km from Kilauea, 69.6 km from Mauna Loa; 31-37 km from Kilauea summit lava thermal clusters (2-4 km from summit), no wildfire source upwind
Kilauea recently eruptive with pause 2 hr before image is plausible vog source; Mauna Loa not erupting

overall.rule: most hazardous class with confidence >= 0.70 (wildfire_smoke > vog_* > dust > cloud)
